objective: Vulnerability scan reports, compliance findings, and risk scorecards -- and who each one is written for
secondaryObjectives: Action plans (escalation, dependencies) and inhibitors to remediation: contractual agreements, organizational governance, business process interruption, degrading functionality, legacy and proprietary systems

SOC metrics and KPIs: alert volume, false-positive rate, true-positive rate, mean time to close, mean time to detect, mean time to respond, mean time to remediate, percentage of alerts escalated, and alert-to-incident ratio

sources.cite: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-004 Exam Objectives, Exam Objectives Document Version 2.0 (exam launched 2026-06-23; domains 34/26/24/16)
sources.note: Relevant text: 1.2 'Given a scenario, analyze indicators of potential malicious activity' (host-related indicators: resource consumption, unauthorized software, anomalous activity: suspicious or rogue processes, Living Off the Land Binaries (LOLBins) and Scripts, file system changes, data exfiltration); 2.3 'Given a scenario, analyze data to prioritize and mitigate vulnerabilities' (exploitability, active exploitation/threat intelligence, asset value, impact, patch/remediation availability, true/false positives, true/false negatives; CVSS metrics, EPSS); 3.2 'Summarize the incident response process' (containment, recovery); 3.3 'Given a scenario, implement incident response techniques' (triage, establishment of a timeline, determining severity and impact, escalation; isolating affected targets, remediation and verification, release from isolation, performing restoration). Read in the official objectives PDF (the course's officialObjectivesUrl) through a summarizing fetch, and the CompTIA V4 page, on 2026-11-11. CS0-003 retires for English on 2026-12-22. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's alert-triage-lolbin-hunt (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the systems, the findings and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run vulnerability management reporting at Glenhaven Health, a fictional hospital network. The quarter closes in three weeks; the board's risk committee, IT operations and the SOC each expect something from you.
handover: Open: 14,200 findings, 61 critical; 9 criticals are on a radiology system whose vendor contract forbids patching without its approval.
The SOC reports alert volume only.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the committee, unable to read the export, defers its decisions a quarter; the radiology risk stays unaddressed.
Week 3: the unvalidated patch breaks image transfer; radiology falls back to CDs for two days and the vendor refuses support.
Week 4: the SOC hits the target by disabling 30 detection rules, including the one that caught last quarter's intrusion.

scoring.modelReasoning: Vulnerability reporting fits the reader: risk scorecards with trends and decisions for executives, detailed scan reports for operators, findings mapped to controls for auditors. Inhibitors (contracts, legacy systems, business interruption) need an action plan: compensating controls, the dependency chased with dates, and escalation of the residual risk to its owner. SOC KPIs should measure outcomes (MTTD, MTTR, false-positive and alert-to-incident ratios); volume targets are gamed.
